entries.title: I Samuel 10:1
segments: Poured it upon his head; in token of his being set apart and furnished by God to be king of Israel.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:2
segments: Rachel's sepulchre;
See note,

. 
 
If men wait upon God and follow his directions, he will show them what he would have them do, and furnish them for the duties to which he calls them.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:3
segments:
Tabor; or oak of Tabor: not mount Tabor, but a place apparently in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
  Men going up to God; to worship God.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:5
segments:
The hill of God; an eminence on which he was worshipped, and on which was a school of the prophets. 
 
  They shall prophesy; praise God, under divine inspiration, with the voice and instruments of music.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:6
segments: Prophesy with them; compare

. 
 
  Turned into another man; so changed by the influence of God's Spirit as to be fitted to become king.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:7
segments:
As occasion serve; as he should judge best; or as circumstances might require. 
 
If men are under the guidance of God and seek his glory, they will be able to judge, in view of all circumstances, what should be done to render themselves most useful.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:9
segments:
Another heart; one that fitted him to govern the people. 
 
All the qualifications of men for the formation and accomplishment of great and useful plans come from God, and lay them under increased obligations of devotion to his service; but enlarged views and great talents may be given, and men may join externally in the worship of God, without the renewing and sanctifying influences of his Spirit.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:11
segments: Is Saul also among the prophets? they were surprised that, without having been instructed, he should be able thus to join with them.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:12
segments: Their father; the father of the prophets.  This was God, who could endow whomsoever he pleased with the gift of prophecy.  It ought not then to surprise them that Saul was among the prophets.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:19
segments:
Rejected your God; by insisting on a change in the government which he had established. 
 
The reception from God of an object which is sought is no certain evidence of his approbation.  He may give it in wrath.
We should therefore rely upon his wisdom rather than our own, saying, Not my will, but thine be done.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:20
segments: Benjamin was taken; they cast lots, and the lot fell upon the tribe of Benjamin.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:22
segments:
Should yet come thither; or, had yet come thither. 
 
  Stuff; the baggage and other furniture of the assembled people.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:23
segments: Higher than any of the people; personal size and strength were much valued by the ancients in their kings.  God was pleased, in the first instance, to give the people a king after their own ideas, before he gave them one after his own heart.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:25
segments: The manner of the kingdom; the regulations which God had prescribed for its government.
Kings, and men in authority, as well as in all other conditions of life, are bound to be acquainted with and to be governed by the revealed will of God.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:26
segments: Had touched; inclined by his Spirit to follow Saul and support his authority.

entries.title: I Samuel 10:27
segments: The best way to treat difficulties often is, for a time at least, to say and do nothing about them.
